chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from al-Haytham ibn ʿUrwah al-Tamīmī, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about His, Exalted is He, saying:
“So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows.”

So he said: “Its revelation is not like that; rather it is: ‘So wash your faces and your hands from the elbows.’” Then he passed his hand from his elbow to his fingers. According to this reading, the question falls away from its very basis.

As for the report that Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, who said: One who saw Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام at Minā informed me that he was wiping the top of his feet from the upper part of the foot to the ankle, and from the ankle to the upper part of the foot.
Then it is restricted to wiping the two feet and does not extend to the head and the two hands, and that also indicates this.

key_terms.أَيْدِيَكُمْ: Your hands; the limb discussed in relation to the direction of washing.
key_terms.الْكَعْبِ: The ankle; the endpoint mentioned in the description of wiping the feet.
key_terms.الْمَرَافِقِ: The elbows; the boundary point for washing the hands in wudu (ablution).
key_terms.ظَهْرَ قَدَمَيْهِ: The tops of his feet; the area mentioned in the wiping report.
key_terms.فَاغْسِلُوا: Wash; the imperative command in the wudu (ablution) verse.
key_terms.مِرْفَقِهِ: His elbow; the starting point demonstrated by the Imam عليه السلام in washing.
key_terms.وُجُوهَكُمْ: Your faces; the first limb mentioned in the wudu (ablution) command.
key_terms.يَمْسَحُ: He was wiping; describing the action performed on the feet.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the wudu (ablution) verse regarding washing the hands and wiping the feet?
ai.summary: This report discusses the wording of the wudu (ablution) verse and its implication for how the hands are washed, indicating washing from the elbows down to the fingers. It also distinguishes a separate report about wiping the feet, clarifying that its manner applies specifically to the feet and not to the head or hands.
